::: {#rem-turing-machine-steps}
#### Steps and running time

The [running time](p-and-np.qmd#def-running-time) of a [Turing machine](#def-turing-machine)
counts the steps of @def-turing-machine,
one application of the transition function each.
One step moves each head by at most one cell,
so reaching a cell $m$ cells away takes at least $m$ steps.
An ordinary computer can jump to any memory address in one operation,
so a Turing machine can need more steps than an ordinary program for the same task.
@thm-tm-robustness and @rem-church-turing explain why that gap does not change
which problems have [polynomial-time](p-and-np.qmd#def-running-time) algorithms.

:::
